title: per-record-reconciliation-tokens-and-deferred-ack-model-for-multi-sink-audit-shipping
creator: Monica Reyes
description:
Problem: Our current audit shipping model emits tenant-scoped events to multiple external sinks (SIEMs, Splunk/HEC, Datadog, webhook subscribers) using batch-level acks and best-effort retries. This leads to three recurring operational problems: 1) inability for customers to reconcile which exact events were accepted by each sink (forensic/compliance use cases), 2) duplicate events or reordering when sinks partially accept batched payloads or time out, and 3) high storage/transfer cost from conservative retry strategies.

Proposed solution: Introduce per-record reconciliation tokens (PRTs) + an optional deferred-ack API for sinks. Each emitted audit record receives a short, signed reconciliation token that uniquely identifies the record version (event_id + generation). We attach the token to the event body and/or as an HTTP header for webhook/HEC transports. Sinks may respond with: 1) per-record ack (fast path), 2) batch-level ack with highest-seen token + bitmap/summary (deferred-ack path), or 3) negative ack with DLQ reason. Server maintains a compact per-tenant token index that maps tokens -> append-offset and short metadata. A separate reconciliation service exposes APIs and dashboards for customers and operators to: query which tokens were acknowledged by a sink, compute missing/duplicate sets, and trigger targeted replays.

Key design/facts: token format is base64(HMAC_SHA256(event_id || generation || tenant_id || timestamp)[:20]) to keep tokens ~28 chars. Tokens are opaque to sinks but verifiable by Redwood when reconciling. Per-tenant HMAC keys are stored in KMS and rotated quarterly. Tokens are stable across harmless retries but change if an event is mutated (generation increment), enabling simple change detection. Deferred-acks allow sinks to reduce request rate: they can ack up to a high-water-mark token and optionally include a 64-bit Bloom summary to signal accepted subset. We accept both explicit lists (small batches) and summaries (large batches) to balance wire size and precision.

Trade-offs: additional payload (~32-64 bytes per record) and indexing storage versus strong reconciliation guarantees and lower long-term retry cost. Signed tokens add CPU to HEC/webhook paths; we mitigate via vectorized HMAC implementation and token caching for hot events. Deferred-ack summary approach introduces probabilistic false-positives (Bloom) and must be surfaced to customers with confidence intervals.

Compatibility: Implementation will be backward-compatible: legacy sinks continue to receive events without tokens until they opt in; tokens are attached in a backward-compatible header (X-Redwood-Audit-Token) with an opt-in header negotiation. For Splunk HEC and Datadog we will provide SDK/adapter examples that read/forward tokens in preferred fields.

Observability & SLAs: Add new metrics per-sink and per-tenant: reconcile_ack_rate, reconcile_missing_count, duplicate_detection_rate, token_index_size, reconcile_query_latency. Add trace points for token generation, verification, and reconciliation queries. Define SLOs for reconciliation API (p95 < 300ms) and for token retention queries (p95 < 1s for last 30 days).

Rollout plan: 1) spike & benchmark token generation (Q1) -> completed. 2) implement token generation + per-tenant index + KMS integration behind feature flag for Dedicated/Private (opt-in). 3) add deferred-ack protocol on forwarder with adapters for Splunk/HEC and Datadog; enable for a small set of pilot customers. 4) expand to Hosted tenants after 6-week pilot and infra capacity verification.

Security: tokens are HMAC-signed, KMS key management, token exposure limited to delivery paths, rotation strategy planned, and security review required before outbound GA.

Success criteria: customers can produce reconciliation reports showing <1% unknown events in the target window and duplicate rates reduced by 70% for opt-in sinks. Expected storage increase: ~10% for token index per tenant on average; expected bandwidth reduction from fewer retries >20% for pilot sinks.
acceptance_criteria: Per-record tokens are generated and verifiable via internal API
Forwarders attach X-Redwood-Audit-Token header for opt-in sinks
Deferred-ack protocol implemented with both explicit-list and Bloom-summary modes
Reconciliation service can report acked/missing/duplicated tokens per tenant and per sink
Integration tests with Splunk HEC and Datadog endpoints pass simulated partial-acceptance and timeout scenarios
Feature gated rollout path exists and can be toggled per-tenant without downtime
implementation_steps: Spike: benchmark HMAC token generation and caching (completed)
Schema: add token field to audit proto and header negotiation field
KMS: provision per-tenant HMAC keys and rotation API
Index: implement compact append-only token index with snapshotting and TTL
Forwarder: add token emission and deferred-ack HTTP paths
Adapters: release Splunk/Datadog adapter examples and webhook header docs
Reconciliation service: query API, UI dashboard, and reconciliation job to compute diffs
E2E tests: build failure injection harness and load tests
Pilot rollout: enable for 3 tenants and monitor metrics for 6 weeks
Security review and privacy signoff before GA
notes: We must coordinate with Solutions and Support for pilot onboarding. Consider providing a one-click export of reconciliation reports for compliance teams. Monitor storage growth and consider compression of token index snapshots.
comments: 2025-01-20: Spike results show HMAC_SHA256 token generation at 120k/s per core with AVX2 optimizations.
2025-01-28: Design review feedback: make Bloom-summary optional and include false-positive rate in response metadata.
2025-02-05: Security requested explicit threat model for token leakage; added KMS rotation notes.
2025-02-14: Integration test harness added for Splunk HEC partial-acceptance simulation (PR #309).
2025-02-19: Pilot tenants identified: finance-platform-1, compliance-saas-2, enterprise-beta-3. Scheduled onboarding calls next week.
